item.title: Seniors embrace Tesla automated driving technology despite questions about safety
item.description:
Transportation
Seniors embrace Tesla automated driving technology despite questions about safety
November 23, 20265:00 AM ET
Joel Rose
Joan Spalding, 89, sits behind the wheel of her Tesla Model Y, equipped with Full-Self Driving (Supervised) technology, on a recent drive near her home in Evergreen, Colo.
Jimena Peck for NPR
hide caption
toggle caption i
Jimena Peck for NPR
EVERGREEN, Colo. — Joan Spalding has driven the steep, winding road that leads to her house outside Denver for more than 50 years. But these days, the 89-year-old barely touches the steering wheel or the pedals.
Instead she tells the car where she wants to go, and presses a button on the large touch-screen in the dashboard of her Tesla Model Y.
"I just get in and go," Spalding says.
For all practical purposes, the car appears to be driving itself, navigating confidently on twisting roads through postcard valleys full of juniper and ponderosa pine.
"Now this is probably one of the narrowest roads," Spalding says, as the car pulls onto a dirt track that can barely fit two cars side by side, with a steep drop off to one side.
The Tesla handles the tight turns gracefully, even stopping to let an SUV squeeze by in the other lane.

item.title: Do not feed the animals. Vets explain why hats, coins and shoes can be deadly.
item.description:
National
Do not feed the animals. Vets explain why hats, coins and shoes can be deadly.
November 22, 20268:53 PM ET
By
Chandelis Duster
Fiona, a Nile Hippopotamus, eats her specialty birthday cake to celebrate turning three-years old this Friday, in her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden, Thursday, Jan. 23, 2020, in Cincinnati.
John Minchillo/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
John Minchillo/AP
The death of Fiona, a beloved hippopotamus who captured hearts, has renewed calls to remind zoo visitors that animals can die from swallowing foreign objects.
Fiona, 9 years old, died Thursday after ingesting a hat that accidentally ended up in her habitat at the Cincinnati Zoo. The zoo said that the hat was lodged in the hippo's small intestine and surgery was not possible.
"Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn't fight anymore," Cincinnati Zoo Director Dave Jenike said in a statement.
While deaths are rare, items such as coins, shoes and sunglasses frequently fall, and sometimes are tossed, into animal enclosures.

item.title: Meet the young authors! A literacy program inspires kids in South Africa
item.description:
Meet the young authors! A literacy program inspires kids in South Africa
November 22, 202612:34 PM ET
By
Kate Bartlett
Fiona Mogane, 13, contributed the story "Lindani's Modelling Journey" to From Gomora to the World. Stories from Alex, a new book of short stories written by kids who are part of the "Read Alex" literacy program in Johannesburg. Participants in weekly classes wrote stories drawing on their own lives.
Madalene Cronje for NPR
hide caption
toggle caption i
Madalene Cronje for NPR
JOHANNESBURG — It's an ordinary Saturday morning in Alexandra township, known simply as Alex or sometimes dubbed Gomora, a reference to the biblical city of Gomorrah that was known for its wickedness.
That nickname stems from Alexandra's high crime rates. It's a high-density area, where modest brick houses and tin shacks stretch as far as the eye can see and rotting garbage piles up along potholed streets.
But that image doesn't intrude on an event at a small building at the Kwabhekilanga Sports Ground. There's a palpable sense of excitement. Something different is happening this weekend and community members have turned up for it.
